newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico opens bidding for northern warehouses.
newsitem.headline: Mexico opens bidding for northern warehouses.

text.p: Mexico's Finance Ministry announced Monday via local newspapers that it had opened bidding to privatize a package of warehouses based mainly in the north of Mexico.
Grouped under the company Seranor, the package is one of three privatizations of storage houses the government intends to move into private hands this year.
The government plans to sell the warehouses' assets in addition to partial usage rights of silos based in the port city of Guaymas in Sonora state, the ministry said.
It did not say how many warehouses were grouped in the Seranor package.

It added that the government will give preference to consortium that have at least a 20 percent stake from "a national agriculture producing group." Foreign investment in the warehouses will be limited to 49 percent, the ministry said.
Bids will be due Sept. 12, with a decision expected within 15 working days.
The winner of the privatization of the recently privatized southern chain of warehouses will not be eligible to bid for the northern sites, the ministry added.
Mexican builder Empresas ICA offered 620 million pesos for the southern warehouses, known as Alsur.
